newsitem.title: USA: GM's Saturn unit turned first-ever net profit in 1996.
newsitem.headline: GM's Saturn unit turned first-ever net profit in 1996.

text.p: General Motors Corp Chairman Jack Smith said Tuesday that Saturn Corp. reported its first ever net profit in 1996 since the division started selling cars in 1990.
"It gets better and better all the time," Smith said of Saturn's financial performance.
Talking to reporters at the North American International Auto Show, Smith called Saturn a success, although he said it needs more production capacity.
"As we look at it today, they're successful. They need to grow, and we have facilities that are available so we want to use those facilities," Smith said.
Saturn, originally formed in 1984, has created a niche for itself as an owner-friendly brand where consumers can purchase a car without haggling over the price.
In the past, Saturn has been profitable on an operating basis, but not after the annual amortization of GM's original $5 billion investment was included.

At a press conference, Saturn officials said as of the end of last year 76 customers had taken delivery of the new EV1 electric car. There were 29 orders that had been submitted but not delivered, and 469 people have shown various stages of interest in the car, Saturn executives said.
"We have been taken by the depth of interest by buyers," said Joseph Kennedy, Saturn's head of sales and marketing.

Saturn President Donald Hudler declined to comment on sourcing for the new upscale Innovate sedan the division is developing, although he said it would have a high level of North American content. The car is based on the Vectra car from GM's Adam Opel AG unit.
Hudler said the new engine being developed for the car will only be used in the Innovate.
